strategy: Add a generic, read-before-write Starter verifier and installer that reuses the existing Project, Skill, Workflow, Composition, capability, and Provider parsers. Bundle a customer-agent starter with overall audit, module audit, architecture review, repair-and-prove, repair-with-CI, and full-development Workflows plus standards/context extension overlays. Installation copies only a pre-verified declaration package and never modifies customer application source.

changes.responsibility: parse closed starter manifests, verify cross-file identities and provider coverage, list built-ins, and safely install a verified package
changes.reason: package-level integrity and initialization are the proven missing boundary

changes.responsibility: expose starter-list, starter-verify, and starter-init through the portable root authoring command
changes.reason: users and Hosts need one deterministic interface instead of manual file copying

changes.responsibility: publish the closed manifest and entrypoint contract
changes.reason: starter inventory must be reviewable, versioned, and maintainable without ChatGPT

changes.responsibility: provide the customer-agent Project declaration, domain Skill contracts, Workflows, Composition overlays, and package manifest
changes.reason: the requested real project example requires coherent executable declarations

changes.responsibility: prove package verification, all Workflow compilation, overlay composition, Provider coverage, safe installation, and negative paths
changes.reason: starter coherence must be deterministic rather than asserted by documentation

changes.responsibility: document commands, files, interaction mapping, extension examples, CI choices, and standalone application boundary
changes.reason: operators need concrete usage from natural language through generated declarations

unchanged_boundaries: WorkflowSpec and workflow_graph_contract remain the sole runtime/topology authorities
harness_composition remains the sole extension overlay transformer
Capability Registry and Provider Registry remain the source of Provider coverage truth
Starter installation does not activate Providers, grant writes, execute commands, or run Workflows
TaskRun remains the only completion authority and Graph END still means VALIDATING
existing Write Authority Guard and explicit host authorization remain mandatory
customer application source is neither generated nor modified by this starter package
forbidden_repairs: Do not add a second customer-agent runtime or graph interpreter.
Do not install into a non-empty target or follow symlinks from a starter package.
Do not accept absolute, traversal, duplicate, missing, or undeclared manifest paths.
Do not treat configured Provider coverage as Provider activation or write authorization.
Do not put merge authority in the customer-agent full-development Workflow.
Do not make the produced customer application import Harness code.
required_invariants: the starter manifest is closed, versioned, and uses bounded relative paths
every Skill, Workflow, and Composition declaration is validated by the existing canonical parser
Skill and Workflow identities are unique across the package
Project defaults and starter entrypoints resolve to base or derived Workflow IDs
every required capability has an explicit Project Provider binding supported by the current Provider Registry
mutating Workflows remain WRITE and write_governed and never bypass the existing Guard
the CI Workflow creates and waits for a PR check but does not merge it
starter-init verifies before copying and refuses non-empty destinations
the installed package is byte-identical to the bundled declarations

focused: the bundled customer-agent starter verifies all declarations and entrypoints
standards and context overlays compose through harness_composition
starter-init installs a byte-identical package and the installed package re-verifies
counterexamples: duplicate identities, missing files, undeclared entrypoints, and traversal paths are rejected
missing or incompatible Provider bindings are rejected
a non-empty installation target is rejected
regression: Authoring and Composition tests remain green
Workflow Registry, activation, and bootstrap tests remain green
negative_path: starter verification has no execution or authorization effect
full-development Workflow contains no merge capability or merge node
installed declarations contain no dependency from customer application source to Harness runtime

risks: A starter could become a hidden runtime registry; it is restricted to declaration verification and copying.
Default Python commands may not match every project; users can replace the Project declaration through the existing project-init command without editing domain Workflows.
GitHub-specific defaults reduce portability; Provider IDs remain isolated in Project configuration while Workflows request provider-neutral capabilities.
Domain Skills may hide policy assumptions; contracts expose artifacts, capabilities, modes, and extension points for review.
rollback_plan: Remove the starter controller route, manifest schema, bundled customer-agent package, tests, and documentation together. Existing Authoring, Composition, Workflow runtime, Provider adapters, TaskRun, and customer application source require no rollback.
